people.paul.role: Writer who sent Timothy and longs to see the Thessalonians
people.paul.relations: He writes with Silvanus and Timothy. He sent Timothy to the Thessalonians.
people.paul.meaning: Paul recalls how he and his team worked among the Thessalonians. He says Satan hindered his visits. He sent Timothy to learn about their faith. Timothy’s good news comforts Paul. Paul asks that the letter be read to all the brothers.
people.silas.role: Co-sender named with Paul and Timothy
people.silas.relations: The letter names him second, between Paul and Timothy.
people.silas.meaning: The letter names Silvanus in the opening line with Paul and Timothy. The letter says “we” after that. It says nothing else about him by name.
people.timothy.role: Co-sender whom Paul sent to the Thessalonians
people.timothy.relations: He is named with Paul and Silvanus. Paul calls him our brother and God’s servant.
people.timothy.meaning: Paul sends Timothy to establish and comfort the Thessalonians in their faith. Timothy comes back with glad news of their faith and love. The news comforts Paul in his distress and affliction.
people.jesus.role: Lord who rose from the dead and will come
people.jesus.relations: Paul calls him the Lord Jesus Christ and God’s Son. He says God raised him from the dead.
people.jesus.meaning: Paul says the Thessalonians wait for God’s Son from heaven. Paul says Jesus died and rose again. He says the dead in Christ will rise first. He tells the readers to comfort one another with these words.
places.thessalonica.summary: The letter is addressed to the assembly of the Thessalonians in chapter 1. Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy greet them.
places.thessalonica.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.athens.summary: Paul says in chapter 3 that he stayed at Athens alone. From there he sent Timothy to the Thessalonians.
places.athens.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.philippi.summary: In chapter 2 Paul says he and his team suffered at Philippi. They were shamefully treated. Then they told the Thessalonians the Good News.
places.philippi.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
sources.web.summary: All five chapters are the main text for original close readings.
sources.web.limits: The guide did not check dates, manuscripts, or Greek forms. It did not check why the visits were blocked. It did not match the letter with Acts into one full account. The accusations in chapter two are part of the letter’s conflict. They are not independent evidence against all Jewish people. No return date is given.
sources.carr-thessalonians.summary: Carr reads the remembered conduct as a defense of the teachers’ trustworthiness.
sources.carr-thessalonians.limits: This is Carr’s own reading. The guide did not check his Greek analysis or his manuscript choice of infants. It did not check his ancient teacher comparisons or the books he cites. The chosen WEB wording is unchanged.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-43.summary: The lesson studies sincere teaching, growing holiness, and useful work.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-43.limits: First Thessalonians coverage follows what the lesson discusses in chapters one through four. The lesson does not discuss chapter five on its own. The guide did not check the linked hymns, talks, or Restoration passages.
sources.net-thessalonica.summary: The dictionary places the city on the Thermaic Gulf and gives coordinates.
sources.net-thessalonica.limits: Only the opening place description and the coordinates support the marker. The guide did not check old population figures, wider history, inscriptions, buildings, or routes.
sources.atlas-canaan.summary: This Church-published atlas names towns and regions in Canaan.
sources.atlas-canaan.limits: It supplies only the chosen reference coordinates. The earlier review record is unchanged. This source does not confirm Gospel events or exact routes.
sources.net-acts-map.summary: Opening descriptions and coordinates mark the cities named in Acts.
sources.net-acts-map.limits: These broad points do not confirm ancient events, travel paths, buildings, or coastlines. The guide did not adopt older encyclopedia claims about authorship, law, population, or exact dates.
chapters.*.mapNote: Markers show the city addressed and the cities Paul names from his past work.
chapters.*.routeEvidence: The letter gives no travel route and no full list of visits.
